Standalone compile-retention protocols v1 and v2

These are separate measurement campaigns, not retries or replacements of the published v0.4/QMAP/Cirq records. New creation uses locked QCEC 3.10.2 and suite pilot-compile-retention-v2-qcec3102-420s-check60. Sealed v1 uses QCEC 3.10.1 and pilot-compile-retention-v1-420s-check60; its evidence, lock and reader semantics remain intact. The reader requires the exact suite, policy and verifier pairing, not an interchangeable list of supported verifier versions. Protocol revisions 1/2, spec/result/seal format 3 and the partial-raw score version are separate axes. The historical mixed-source report remains authoritative for its own campaigns.

Diagnostic evidence

The historical QCEC 3.10.1 diagnostic (diagnostics/compile-retention/index.html, linked from the navigation of published documentation) shows all 18 frozen identities and links every saved QASM, native QPY and compile manifest. All 54 repeats were committed; all 54 checks reached their hard timeout, so the result is verification incomplete, not an explicit mismatch. The input and outputs have 90 two-qubit gates and two-qubit-only depth 20. One-qubit counts range from 597 to 666, including 647/654/666 at L4; full depths range from 97 to 102. This evidence is separate from the 13-configuration root publication and does not change its selector, historical data or scores.

The separately selected QCEC 3.10.2 v2 diagnostic (diagnostics/compile-retention-v2-qcec3102/index.html) contains the approved fresh run of the same 18 identities and 54 trials. All 54 native bundles were saved. Verification returned 51 no_information criteria; three calls raised the API hard timeout. No outer hard cutoff occurred. All 18 jobs remain verification_incomplete, with zero strict accepts, explicit mismatches, errors or incomplete compilations. A returned inconclusive criterion is a finished API call, not a proof of equivalence. Verification wall time totals 1,642.310 seconds (median 27.111, range 21.074 to 59.157 seconds). Shared-host times are diagnostic, not a matched-host speed comparison with v1.

Run uv run build_site.py to regenerate both the root report and diagnostic pages. Each diagnostics/*/report.json selects one exact sealed FileMap independently of publication.json. Archived measurement source remains frozen; the page template and documentation are display-only and are regenerated by the current builder.

Workspace and ordered schedule

# Inspect campaign.json, including its ordered schedule, before running.
# With the same locked Python environment, run the copied workspace once:
/path/to/locked/python /path/to/new/workspace/atlas.py retention-run

The default campaign extracts exactly 18 published timeout identities: QASMBench Ising n10, BQSKit L2/L3/L4, line/all-to-all, seeds 7/19/43. A canonical schedule is shuffled with seed 20261004 and stored before execution. There are 54 scheduled repeats. No resume, selective retry or favorable-results reuse is allowed. Jobs and checks run sequentially, without overlapping tests or other agent-controlled heavy work. On a shared host the timings are diagnostic, not matched-host performance comparisons.

Target and pipelines

The existing atlas.compile_once recipes, input-width targets and timer boundaries are unchanged. The whole job, including startup, import, export, saving and checks, has one monotonic 420-second deadline. All three compilations precede verification. Each fresh QCEC child gets the lesser of 60 seconds and remaining job time; QCEC's cooperative timeout remains 20 seconds. An exhausted budget starts no child. Cleanup/admin time is recorded separately; it does not extend the result deadline.

QCEC 3.10.2 hard-timeout decision

V2 uses the released mqt.qcec.verify_with_hard_timeout API (#818). The installed 3.10.2 source and executable probes confirmed a separate Python worker, QPY transport of QuantumCircuit inputs including scalar phase, a JSON-style result with top-level equivalence, TimeoutError on expiry and RuntimeError on worker failure. Unlike ordinary verify, it returns a dict, not a Results object; DD counterexamples are not returned. Strict preparation, checker options and accepted criteria are unchanged. The legacy worker continues to use ordinary verify.

The parent persists one absolute cutoff computed from a single monotonic clock sample. Startup, imports, native validation, circuit preparation, serialization and reply publication all consume this same check/job budget. Immediately before the API call the child computes remaining time and subtracts a fixed 1-second receipt reserve inside the cap. If no positive inner duration remains, no API worker is started. The reserve permits an inner timeout reply to become durable; it is frozen in the v2 policy, not added time or a configurable retry allowance. The API's own timer excludes caller-side QPY serialization and may be delayed by process creation, so it cannot replace the outer absolute deadline.

A real instrumented upstream worker that spawned a grandchild confirmed that upstream timeout kills/reaps its direct worker, but can return while the descendant survives. The outer process-group kill/subreaper is therefore retained on normal completion as well as timeout, exceptions and cancellation. It also bounds caller serialization and wins over any late reply. The API alone is not a process-tree or whole-job deadline guarantee. See design rationale.

QASM and actual native QPY are saved create-only with compile time, raw metrics, logical-to-physical initial/final maps in input declaration order, scalar phase, input/source hashes and artifact hashes. File and directory fsync precede the last-published compile manifest, the bundle's commit marker. An uncommitted orphan is forensic evidence, not a measured repeat. QCEC reloads native QPY, never a QASM re-import that might change scalar phase or numerical representation.

The parent owns one child process group at a time. Normal exit, timeout, exceptions and cancellation kill the group, wait for the direct child, reap adopted descendants through a Linux subreaper and confirm group disappearance before proceeding. Uninterruptible OS I/O, a descendant escaping with setsid, supervisor SIGKILL and host failure are outside this guarantee. A hard deadline is a kill-decision bound, not a mathematical completion-time guarantee.

Classification and scoring

Primary precedence is error > compile_incomplete > not_equivalent > verification_incomplete > passed. Individual mixed facts are retained. Only QCEC not_equivalent is an explicit mismatch. equivalent and equivalent_up_to_global_phase are strictly accepted. no_information, equivalent_up_to_phase, probably_equivalent and probably_not_equivalent are unfinished verification, not demonstrated mismatch. A hard timeout or no remaining budget is also unfinished. V2 distinguishes qcec_hard_timeout (API expiry), check_budget (no positive inner duration after the receipt reserve), hard_timeout (outer cutoff) and job_budget (no remaining job time). A check window exhausted while publishing its start receipt is not spawned; its actual no-start observation authenticates check_budget, even if the earlier receipt recorded positive time. Completion is judged at the post-wait observation, not an earlier poll before possible scheduler preemption. Timeout replies carry no invented QCEC criterion or acceptance. Crashes, malformed replies, export/I/O failures and unknown criteria are errors. Passing requires three committed compiles and three strict accepts.

Output rules (basis, coupling, width, maps, phase) are independent of equivalence. Raw medians use available committed repeats and show n/3 coverage. Unfinished verification remains in the scheduled seed-slot denominator and contributes zero to the pass numerator. It does not itself make a score N/A. Quality and Speed each require their necessary raw and reference measurements; missing required cases are not silently excluded. Partial-repeat scoring is separately named qcec-adjusted-partial-v2; historical qcec-adjusted-v1 values are unchanged. The 18-job diagnostic has no reference rows, so normalized scores are N/A and only raw measurements/coverage are informative. This is not an approximation track.

Seal and publication

Standalone kind=compile-retention uses spec, result schema and seal version 3. The seal freezes source commit and byte inventory, lock and resolved versions, inputs and corpus license, recipe and checker settings, deadlines, transport and ordering policy, schedule, host/affinity/thread settings and UTC/monotonic facts. Execution identities include recipe, input, verifier/environment, source and policy. The same display configuration ID does not imply the same execution identity.

Before sealing, the maintained reader re-derives native metrics, map/phase/output rules, hashes, check classifications, job precedence, medians and raw rows from all scheduled terminal facts without re-running QCEC. Every referenced file and forensic log/orphan is in the exact snapshot inventory. MEASUREMENT_COMPLETE authenticates the create-only snapshot and is published last. A complete schedule of unsuccessful checks can be sealed; a cancelled/incomplete schedule, corrupt bundle or tampered file cannot. A seal means complete evidence, not all passed.

A FileMap must cover exactly every sealed file plus marker and snapshot. It cannot backfill old rows or merge these identities into the existing mixed-source campaign. The approved QCEC 3.10.2 rerun adds a new standalone campaign archive, QASM, QPY, manifests, logs, raw data, exact FileMap and a separate diagnostic selector beside v1. It covers only the same 18 identities, each with three trials. Existing historical bytes and scores stay unchanged. Local sealing, archiving or previewing is not authorization to push, create a PR or change the root publication selector.

Raw data and the input manifest are separate from the display-only configuration notes.
